title: Riemann integral
summary: The Riemann integral is the common limit approached by every sufficiently fine tagged sum.

context.framework: Riemann integration on compact real intervals
context.note: Revision 2 gives one precise Riemann formulation; other integration theories require separate formulation objects.

assumptions.text: The domain is a compact interval [a,b] in the real numbers.

content.plain: Cut an interval into sufficiently short pieces, sample the function in each piece, and add height times width; one stable limiting value is the Riemann integral.
content.exact: A bounded f:[a,b]→R is Riemann-integrable with integral I iff for every ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that every tagged partition a=x₀<⋯<xₙ=b with tᵢ∈[xᵢ₋₁,xᵢ] and mesh maxᵢ(xᵢ−xᵢ₋₁)<δ satisfies |Σᵢ f(tᵢ)(xᵢ−xᵢ₋₁)−I|<ε.
content.example: For f(x)=x on [0,1], the Riemann integral is 1/2.
content.caveat: Lebesgue, stochastic, contour, and path integrals are distinct constructions and must not be folded into this exact formulation.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Replaces a mixed Riemann/Lebesgue synopsis with one scoped exact formulation. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
